facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's Annual Health Service Performance Report 2024 states that the HMIS, on the web-based DHIS2 platform, stores the Ministry's aggregated routine health service data and is managed within its Department of Policy, Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation (Health Information System unit), with the Ministry's ICT Unit supporting the platform; DHIS2 was set up by the Ministry 'through its partners'.

The Ministry states that every health facility, public and private, is required under the 1976 Public Health Law to report monthly service utilisation data, that counties must submit complete routine data to the central Ministry by the 17th of the following month, and that the 2024 report compares all counties on aggregated routine data reported through DHIS2 (4.1 million consultations in 2024); it describes facility reporting completeness and timeliness as 'remarkable' but the passages give no rate, and do not say at which tier the data is keyed.

The Ministry's ICT Unit reports that during 2024 some data in the Ministry's DHIS2 system was lost, affecting several programme areas and forcing data officers to re-enter health data; it recommends more backup servers and a formal disaster recovery plan.

systems.owner: Ministry of Health, Department of Policy, Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation
systems.tiers: all health facilities, public and private, required to report monthly; counties submit to the central Ministry

note: Passages file: only paragraphs carrying a study term were read, so reporting-rate tables in the full report were not seen. The tiers fact rests on a legal reporting requirement and county comparisons, not on a statement of which tiers enter data; the parent may prefer to drop it. The report also says the unit coordinated interoperability of the Ministry's information systems, with no detail. LIS and HRIS appear only in the abbreviations.
